public_health_question.v: How did the percentage of U.S. adults aged ≥25 years meeting both federal muscle-strengthening and aerobic physical activity guidelines in 2022 vary by educational attainment?

ev.q: Who Met the 2018 Federal Physical Activity Guidelines for Both Muscle-Strengthening and Aerobic Physical Activity, § by Educational Attainment — United States, 2022
The muscle-strengthening guideline was met if the respondent reported performing muscle-strengthening activities on ≥2 days per week.
Estimates are based on household interviews of a sample of the civilian, noninstitutionalized U.S. population
Source: National Center for Health Statistics, National Health Interview Survey, 2022.
Source: National Center for Health Statistics, National Health Interview Survey, 2022.

equity.level_reason: Percentages are reported and described by educational attainment (an SES dimension), rising from 12.2% to 33.6%, but no difference or ratio is computed and the gradient is not framed or interpreted as a disparity.

level_alternative.reason: Education is the sole exposure and a social determinant, so the described gradient (12.2% vs 33.6%) could meet level 3 under the social-determinant exposure rule without the word disparity.

ev.q: The percentage of adults who met these guidelines increased with increasing educational attainment

equity.equity_measurement: Education is the SES proxy; the population is restricted to adults aged ≥25 years; only the extreme education groups are cited in the text.

notes: NHIS estimates are presumably survey-weighted, but weighting is not stated, so no weighting procedure is recorded. The guidelines define the outcome, not a comparison referent.
